z44mb1:579: Thread scheduler: responsible for managing and dispatching the execution of thread blocks. It assigns thread blocks to appropriate CUDA cores based on their resource requirements (such as registers and shared memory) and execution state. When a thread block is paused waiting for memory data, the thread scheduler switches to another ready thread block to continue execution, improving SM utilization. For GPUs, there are several storage hierarchy levels. From top to bottom, read speed decreases while capacity increases: when a GPU thread needs to read data, it first looks in the L1 cache; if not found, it goes to the L2 cache; if still not found, it finally goes to HBM. If we can use data organization strategies to make threads more likely to find the data they need in the L1/L2 cache, we can improve data read speed. This echoes the title: why optimize matrix multiplication for L2 cache hits. Before explaining L2 cache hit optimization for matrix multiplication, we need to emphasize the concept of the block again. Triton is programmed around the abstract logic of blocks. Work inside a block is carried out by multiple threads, and threads share shared memory, but it is not entirely equivalent to a GPU thread block. GPU thread blocks are more "physical": in CUDA programming, you must manually manage thread block dimensions, indices, and other details. Triton blocks are more "logical": the Triton compiler automatically handles many hardware-related scheduling and optimizations, so developers only need to focus on the block's compute logic and data processing.
